prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: []
1: ["Creating Your Desktop Pet", "Tip: Right-click your pet on the desktop anytime to open quick interactions."]
2: ["Desktop Display Readiness", "Checking screen permissions so your pet can roam freely on your desktop.", "Launch Desktop Pet"]
3: ["Listen to Pet Voice"]
4: ["Signing in with your existing account automatically restores all your previously adopted desktop pets."]
5: ["For best 3D pet accuracy, use a clear front-facing photo with good lighting and no background clutter."]
6: ["Feel free to work on other tasks. We will alert you the moment your pet is ready!"]
7: ["How Would You Like to Meet Your Pet?"]
8: ["Welcome to Desktop Pets", "Adopt an animated pet companion that walks along your taskbar, reacts to your day, and keeps you company."]
9: ["Your Pet is Live on Your Desktop!", "Quick Tips: Click and drag to move your pet, right-click to open options, or double-click to interact."]

verdicts.problem: asks for personal information (photo of user)
